description: Implement the 'What Exists Today' section (investor question 10) as a three-column maturity model showing Already Built, Currently Building, and Future Vision. This section goes after competitive-section in index.html.
steps: Create css/status.css following the BEM pattern from css/competitive.css. The section uses class prefix 'status'. Include: .status-section (hidden by default, revealed via .status--visible), .status__container (max-width: --container-xl, margin auto), .status__intro with heading and description (data-reveal), .status__columns as a CSS Grid (1 column mobile, 3 columns at 1024px), three .status__column cards each with .status__column-header (heading + a subtle label like 'Completed'/'In Progress'/'Planned'), .status__column-items list, .status__item elements within each column. Add a .status__bridge at the bottom for the transition text. All child elements use opacity:0 + translateY with transition, revealed via .status__element--revealed. Include responsive breakpoints at 768px (2-column grid) and 1024px (3-column grid). Include reduced motion media query. Use design tokens from variables.css exclusively - no hardcoded values.

Create js/sections/StatusSection.js following the exact pattern from js/sections/CompetitiveSection.js. The class should: get element by id 'status-section', set up IntersectionObserver for [data-reveal] children, add 'status__element--revealed' class on intersection, implement reveal() (removes aria-hidden, adds status--visible, sets up observer), hide() (adds aria-hidden, removes status--visible, disconnects observer, removes revealed classes), isVisible(), destroy(). Keep methods under 60 lines, class under 400 lines.

Add the HTML section in index.html AFTER the closing </section> of competitive-section and BEFORE </main>. The section has id='status-section', class='status-section', aria-label='What exists today - current development status', aria-hidden='true'. Structure: intro with heading '[What Exists Today]' and description about transparency. Three columns: Column 1 'Already Built' with items: Product architecture, Design system, Technical foundation, Interactive investor experience, Research, AI exploration, MVP planning. Column 2 'Currently Building' with items: Consumer app, Creator app, Admin platform, Backend, AI Matching V1, Trust & Safety, Marketplace foundation. Column 3 'Future Vision' with items: Live Rooms, Creator monetization, AI Companion, Events, Multi-country expansion, Enterprise opportunities. Bridge text: '[Now let's look at where we're going next.]'. All content wrapped in brackets as placeholders per project convention.
Add @import './status.css'; in css/main.css after the @import './competitive.css'; line.

Add import { StatusSection } from './sections/StatusSection.js'; in js/app.js after the CompetitiveSection import. Add instantiation: const statusSection = new StatusSection(); statusSection.reveal(); after the competitiveSection.reveal(); call.
acceptance_criteria: css/status.css exists with BEM-named classes, uses only design tokens, includes responsive breakpoints and reduced-motion support
js/sections/StatusSection.js exists with reveal/hide/destroy lifecycle, IntersectionObserver setup, no function >60 lines, no class >400 lines
index.html contains status-section after competitive-section with three columns of items matching the task specification
js/app.js imports and instantiates StatusSection after CompetitiveSection
Bridge text reads '[Now let's look at where we're going next.]'
No fake checkmarks or inflated claims - items are presented as honest placeholders
Section is accessible with proper aria attributes
verification: Run node --check js/sections/StatusSection.js to validate JS syntax
Confirm status-section appears after competitive-section in index.html via grep
Confirm main.css has the status.css import after competitive.css
Confirm app.js has StatusSection import and instantiation
findings: Implemented successfully. JS passes node --check syntax validation. Section placed after competitive-section (line 1092) and before </main> (line 1166). CSS uses design tokens from variables.css with subtle color differentiation for column maturity stages using rgba values matching brand tokens (success green for built, brand primary for building, brand secondary for future). No hardcoded values for spacing/typography/layout.
